questions.q: Explain in your own words what 'Types of Families: Nuclear Family' refers to.
questions.a: A nuclear family consists of only parents and their children living together in one household.

questions.q: State the single key point to remember about 'Types of Families: Nuclear Family'.
questions.a: A nuclear family is a small unit made up of parents and their unmarried children sharing a home and resources.

questions.q: Under which section is 'Types of Families: Nuclear Family' taught, and from which source text?
questions.a: Types of Families

questions.q: Explain in your own words what 'Types of Families: Joint Family' refers to.
questions.a: A joint family is one in which several generations of a family live together under one roof, sharing resources and responsibilities.

questions.q: State the single key point to remember about 'Types of Families: Joint Family'.
questions.a: A joint family includes grandparents, parents, children, and sometimes uncles, aunts, and cousins living and working together.

questions.q: Under which section is 'Types of Families: Joint Family' taught, and from which source text?
questions.a: Types of Families

questions.q: Explain in your own words what 'Types of Families: Extended Family' refers to.
questions.a: An extended family includes members beyond the nuclear family, such as grandparents, aunts, uncles, and cousins, who may or may not live in the same household.

questions.q: State the single key point to remember about 'Types of Families: Extended Family'.
questions.a: An extended family broadens the family circle to include relatives beyond parents and children, connected by blood or marriage.

questions.q: Under which section is 'Types of Families: Extended Family' taught, and from which source text?
questions.a: Types of Families

concepts.title: Roles and Responsibilities in a Family

questions.q: Explain in your own words what 'Roles and Responsibilities in a Family' refers to.
questions.a: Each member of a family has certain roles and responsibilities that contribute to the smooth functioning and well-being of the household.

questions.q: State the single key point to remember about 'Roles and Responsibilities in a Family'.
questions.a: Family members share duties such as earning, cooking, caring for children, and supporting elders so that the household runs smoothly.

questions.q: Under which section is 'Roles and Responsibilities in a Family' taught, and from which source text?
questions.a: Roles and Responsibilities

questions.q: Explain in your own words what 'Family Values and Traditions' refers to.
questions.a: Family values and traditions are the beliefs, customs, and practices passed down from one generation to the next within a family.

questions.q: State the single key point to remember about 'Family Values and Traditions'.
questions.a: Values such as respect, honesty, and cooperation, along with traditions like festivals and rituals, shape a family's identity.

questions.q: Under which section is 'Family Values and Traditions' taught, and from which source text?
questions.a: Family Values and Traditions

concepts.title: Community and Its Types: Rural and Urban

questions.q: Explain in your own words what 'Community and Its Types: Rural and Urban' refers to.
questions.a: A community is a group of people living together in a particular area who share common interests, customs, and a sense of belonging.

questions.q: State the single key point to remember about 'Community and Its Types: Rural and Urban'.
questions.a: Communities may be rural (villages, based on agriculture) or urban (towns and cities, based on trade and services), each with distinct features.

questions.q: Under which section is 'Community and Its Types: Rural and Urban' taught, and from which source text?
questions.a: Community

questions.q: Explain in your own words what 'Community Participation and Cooperation' refers to.
questions.a: Community participation means members actively taking part in collective activities, while cooperation means working together for common goals.

questions.q: State the single key point to remember about 'Community Participation and Cooperation'.
questions.a: When community members join hands to solve problems, celebrate events, or help neighbours, the community becomes stronger and more united.

questions.q: Under which section is 'Community Participation and Cooperation' taught, and from which source text?
questions.a: Community

questions.q: Explain in your own words what 'Interdependence of Family and Community' refers to.
questions.a: Families and communities depend on each other: families form communities, and communities provide support, services, and a sense of belonging to families.

questions.q: State the single key point to remember about 'Interdependence of Family and Community'.
questions.a: A family is the basic unit of a community, and the community in turn supports families through shared resources, security, and social bonds.

questions.q: Under which section is 'Interdependence of Family and Community' taught, and from which source text?
questions.a: Family and Community

concepts.title: Social Institutions: Family, Community, and School

questions.q: Explain in your own words what 'Social Institutions: Family, Community, and School' refers to.
questions.a: Social institutions are organised structures in society, such as the family, community, and school, that guide behaviour and meet people's needs.

questions.q: State the single key point to remember about 'Social Institutions: Family, Community, and School'.
questions.a: Family, community, and school are key social institutions that teach values, provide support, and prepare children for life in society.

questions.q: Under which section is 'Social Institutions: Family, Community, and School' taught, and from which source text?
questions.a: Social Institutions

questions.q: Explain in your own words what 'Changing Nature of Families' refers to.
questions.a: Families change over time due to factors such as migration, urbanisation, education, and new occupations, leading to shifts from joint to nuclear setups.

questions.q: State the single key point to remember about 'Changing Nature of Families'.
questions.a: Modern influences like city jobs and education have led many families to become smaller and nuclear, while still retaining values and bonds.

questions.q: Under which section is 'Changing Nature of Families' taught, and from which source text?
questions.a: Changing Families
